summary: Console alerts firing despite dashboard showing no metric spike due to filter mismatch
description:
Issue summary: Customer reports that alert rule 'High token rate - Checkout API' fired repeatedly over the last 18 hours, while the dashboard for the same metric (Requests > Token count) shows no corresponding spike for the alerted time windows.

Impact: Multiple noisy alerts caused customer runbook escalation and paging. No user-visible service degradation reported, but alerts are disrupting on-call rotations.

Environment: Production (us-east). Customer has Dedicated plan with reserved capacity; metrics are ingested into our TSDB with 1s granularity and rolled up to 1m.

Observed behavior: Alert history shows thresholds exceeded in three disjoint 5-minute windows. On the dashboard, using default 15m timeframe and the account-scoped filter, there is no spike; visual inspection of raw traces (span latency) does not match the alert windows.

Hypothesis: Alert evaluation uses a different filter set / aggregation window than the dashboard chart (alerting uses the global account filter + 30s evaluation window; dashboard uses dashboard-level widget filters and auto-applied timezone). Possible root causes: filter merging bug in console when constructing alert queries, or a mismatch between the metrics query builder used by chart widgets and the alerting engine.

Requested outcome: Confirm root cause, suppress noisy alerts for this customer's alerting rule until fix, and provide mitigation guidance for customers creating alerts for token-based metrics.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Log into Redwood Console as a customer admin (Acme Retail).
2) Open Dashboards > Checkout Service Overview > Widget: 'Requests > Token count' and set time range to last 1h.
3) Observe steady token rate with small fluctuations; no 5-minute spike visible.
4) Open Alerts > Alert Rules and view rule 'High token rate - Checkout API'.
5) Inspect Alert History and note alert firings at 2026-03-11T22:05Z, 2026-03-12T01:40Z, 2026-03-12T05:10Z.
6) Compare raw metric query in alert definition vs widget query; note differences in 'account_id' filter and 'rollup' parameter.
7) Attach trace samples for the alert windows and verify no corresponding application-level surge.
logs: [2026-03-12T05:10:03Z] alert-evaluator[prod-us-east]: rule_id=4178 fired for account=acme-retail threshold=5000 tokens/min value=5124
[2026-03-12T05:09:59Z] metrics-ingest[prod-us-east]: series token_rate.account=acme-retail value=48.4 per-second (raw), rollup=2904 per-minute
comments: Priya Shah (Support) 2026-03-12: Created ticket after customer posted in #support-acme with screenshots and alert history export.
Daniel Kim (On-call SRE) 2026-03-12: Assigned for investigation; initial hypothesis is filter-stacking causing duplicate account filters in alert backend.
Acme Retail - Ops (Customer) 2026-03-12: 'We only want alerts against production traffic for the Checkout API; current noise is paging our SRE team.'

Daniel Kim (On-call SRE) 2026-03-13: Reproduced locally: dashboard widget query includes explicit 'account_id=acme-retail' but alert engine was implicitly adding both 'account_id' and 'org_id' -> metrics dedup/rollup path returned higher aggregated value.

Priya Shah (Support) 2026-03-13: Provided short-term mitigation: disabled the alert rule and suggested a temporary rule using the dashboard-exported query. Customer accepted; re-enabled with adjusted query at 2026-03-13T14:30Z.
Daniel Kim (On-call SRE) 2026-03-14: Working with Analytics team to validate query builder normalization logic; will attach PR once available.
Analytics eng (Nina Lopez) 2026-03-14: Confirmed discrepancy in how widget-level filters were serialized vs the evaluator; preparing fix to dedupe filters before evaluation.
investigation_notes: Checked alert evaluator logs and metrics ingestion pipeline for the reported alert times; raw ingestion values do not show minute-scale spikes consistent with the alerted values.

Replayed alert evaluation with same inputs in staging: reproduces when both a global account filter and a widget-level account filter are present; the serialization ends up duplicating filters which previously triggered a different aggregation path in the TSDB that yields higher rollups.

Confirmed that alerting backend queries the timeseries-store with rollup=60s by default; dashboard widgets often use rollup=15s or no rollup depending on time range. The serialization bug caused query planner to use 'per-minute' rollups incorrectly.
Unit tests added to reproduce filter-duplication case; baseline confirms that deduping filters in the query builder prevents the inflated values.
Customer-facing impact: noisy alerts only for customers who have both org-level and widget-level scoping (common for enterprise accounts with multiple sub-orgs).
resolution_notes: Mitigation (applied 2026-03-13): Support recommended and implemented a temporary alert rule that exactly mirrors the dashboard-exported metric query (explicit account_id and rollup=60s). Customer accepted and paging paused.

Engineering fix (in progress): Analytics team will merge PR to dedupe serialized filters in alert query builder (PR: https://github.com/redwood/console/pull/2314). Target deployment window: 2026-03-17 US maintenance window.

Post-fix actions: run a sweep to identify alert rules potentially affected (heuristic: rules referencing account/org and using token-based rollups) and notify owners with recommended re-evaluation steps.

Follow-ups: Update alerting-runbook and dashboard docs to call out differences in rollup semantics and recommend exporting dashboard query to seed alert rules. Assigned to Nina Lopez for documentation updates.
Customer communication: Priya to send a bridge summary and expected timeline; include rollback plan if PR causes regression.
